chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Muskam, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the compurgation (sworn endorsements), has the Sunnah flowed regarding it? He said, so he mentioned a hadith similar to the one of Ibn Sinan, and said in his hadith: 'It is the truth, and it is written with us.'

key_terms.ابْنِ سِنَانٍ: Ibn Sinan; a prominent narrator whose hadith is referenced here.
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: Compurgation; a method of proof involving oaths, often used in blood money cases.
key_terms.حَقٌّ: Truth; indicating validity and correctness of the ruling.
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: Sunnah; a established prophetic or imamic tradition or practice.
key_terms.مَكْتُوبَةٌ: Written; recorded or documented in their sources.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compurgation (al-qasamah) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that al-qasamah is not merely a customary practice but a divinely sanctioned legal mechanism ('haqq') with established precedent ('sunnah') within the Ahl al-Bayt's jurisprudence. By referencing the narration of Ibn Sinan, the Imam underscores the continuity of this evidentiary method in resolving cases of homicide where witnesses are scarce, highlighting its status as a written and authoritative source in Shia legal tradition.
